[Open the Jazz ballad style in the Backing Track](../tools/backing-track.html?style=ballad){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## What it is

A slow standard played by a jazz rhythm section: the bass on beats 1 and 3 (a *two-feel*), held chords on
the piano, and brushes stirring the snare or a soft ride. The band leaves room for the melody.

## A little history

The two-feel is older than walking bass. New Orleans and 1920s dance bands put the tuba or string bass on
1 and 3, and when the bass began walking in the 1930s (see [Swing](swing.qmd)), the two-feel stayed on as the
lighter gear: bands play the head of a tune in two and start walking for the solos. On ballads it never
has to leave. Brushes, used on drums since the 1920s, became the ballad sound through drummers such as Jo
Jones and later Philly Joe Jones and Ed Thigpen. Pianists filled the long chords with the rich voicings
that came from Ellington, Billy Strayhorn and later Bill Evans.

## The band's version

- **Bass:** *Two-feel*: root on 1, fifth on 3, now and then a pickup into the next bar.
- **Comping:** long held chords (*pad*).
- **Drums:** quiet time. **Voicings:** rootless, with unmarked extensions.

## Listening

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Coleman Hawkins, *Body and Soul* | 1939 | The tenor ballad everyone learned; the band barely there. |
| Miles Davis, *'Round Midnight* (*'Round About Midnight*) | 1956 | Harmon mute over Paul Chambers in two. |
| Bill Evans Trio, *My Foolish Heart* (*Waltz for Debby*) | 1961 | Paul Motian's brushes; Scott LaFaro's bass. |
| John Coltrane, *Ballads* | 1962 | A whole album of the form; McCoy Tyner's voicings. |
| John Coltrane & Johnny Hartman, *My One and Only Love* | 1963 | Ballad accompaniment behind a singer. |

### More recent

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Tony Bennett & Amy Winehouse, *Body and Soul* | 2011 | The same tune as Hawkins, with a quiet trio under the voices. |
| Laufey, *Valentine* (*Everything I Know About Love*) | 2022 | A jazz-ballad band under a young pop singer. |

## Sources

- Paul Berliner, *Thinking in Jazz* (Chicago, 1994), on the two-feel and on brushes.
- Ted Gioia, *The Jazz Standards* (Oxford, 2012), entries for the tunes above.
